Thanks Marissa  great session. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Priority sensitive items: full PANs, cardholder names, SSNs (where present), and any session tokens (bearer tokens) we see in headers. Trace IDs are OK to retain but we prefer them hashed so they cannot be used to stitch back to other systems.
- Retention: Compliance requires 90 days for full logs, but legal can request up to 7 years for specific investigations. We'd need a way to set retention per-log-type (e.g., redact and keep hashed trace IDs for 90 days, purge raw responses after 7 days unless flagged).
- Storage: For now we'd like logs pushed to our secure S3 bucket (encrypted, KMS-managed). If Redwood can provide push/export + lifecycle policy, that would be ideal.

Would appreciate a suggested config/MAF (mutual action plan) and a short tech session with Rishi.

Hi all,

Thanks  quick technical proposal inline below. Happy to jump on a call to walk through.

Masking rules (proposed)
- PANs: detect via Luhn + regex; redact to last4 by default (e.g., "**** **** **** 1234"). Optionally tokenise with customer-provided token service before persisting.
- Names & SSNs: configurable regex-based redaction + label-based removal for fields marked as PII in your payload schema.
- Bearer tokens / session tokens: strip from headers and requests; persist a hashed token fingerprint (HMAC-SHA256 with per-customer salt) if you need correlation.
- Trace IDs: hash with HMAC-SHA256 using per-customer salt; store only hashed id with no raw mapping persisted.

Retention & export
- Per-log-type retention windows: e.g., raw responses = 7 days, redacted responses = 90 days, hashed trace index = 90 days (configurable).
- Export: Redwood can push logs to your S3 bucket over Kinesis Firehose or S3 Direct Put with server-side KMS (we accept your KMS key ARN for envelope encryption). We also support Redwood-managed encrypted storage for short-term retention.

Performance / guarantees
- Synchronous redaction pipeline: we guarantee redaction before write to any persistent store. This adds ~2-8ms median per-request for typical text payloads; in peak burst scenarios we recommend our sidecar sampling + streaming pipeline to avoid tail latency impact.
- Batching & sampling options to reduce cost without exposing raw PII.

Deliverables by EOD 14 May
- attached: proposed-map-logging-config.yml (sample) and a short note on SLA impact.

Let me know an available slot for a 30-min tech call; I can do Thu 14th 10-11am PT.
